cohort: 422 pregnant women (>30 weeks of gestation) attending an antenatal clinic, divided into a study group with gestational thrombocytopenia (n=211) and a control group with normal platelet counts (n=211).
finding: Pregnancies with gestational thrombocytopenia were associated with a higher risk of adverse feto-maternal outcomes, including low Apgar scores, increased NICU admission rates, intracranial hemorrhage, neonatal death, and other maternal complications.
